The project is in `./app`, and `mvn -B -ntp -DskipTests test-compile` passes there. I did not run the tests, start the app against a model, or call a live model.

**How it was built.** The Quarkus Agents MCP was reachable, so I created the project with `quarkus_create` on Quarkus 3.40.1 with Java 25. The extensions are `rest`, `rest-jackson`, `smallrye-openapi`, `langchain4j-ollama`, `smallrye-fault-tolerance` and `http-problem`. I called `quarkus_skills` for the REST and fault-tolerance extensions before writing code. I did not look up LangChain4j in context7 or `quarkus_skills`. I stopped the dev-mode instance that `quarkus_create` auto-started. I did not `git init` the project, because you said not to commit anything.

**Endpoint.** `POST /classify` takes the ticket as a `text/plain` body and returns JSON like `{"category":"BILLING"}`. The category is one of `BILLING`, `TECHNICAL` or `OTHER`. Blank or over-long (more than 4,000 characters) tickets get a 400. Other escaping exceptions become RFC 9457 problem responses through `http-problem`.

**AI service.** `TicketClassifier` is a `@RegisterAiService` that returns the `Category` enum directly. It uses a named `classifier` model, `qwen3:1.7b` on Ollama with temperature 0. The ticket is wrapped in `<ticket>…</ticket>` and the system message says it is data, not instructions.

**Guardrail and fallback.** `PromptInjectionGuard` rejects oversized input, reserved delimiter markup inside the ticket, and the phrase "ignore previous instructions". A rejected ticket returns a 400. The method has a 60-second `@Timeout` and a `@Fallback` that returns `OTHER`. The fallback skips guardrail rejections. It does not skip model errors, so if Ollama is down the endpoint returns `OTHER` rather than an error.
